# Datasets

The datasets shown here are airborne LiDAR point clouds sourced from the **USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP)** — a nationwide initiative to collect high-quality topographic data across the United States. Data are freely available through the [USGS National Map](https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program).

---

## Urban Forest — Near Central Park, New York City

**Source:** USGS 3DEP · NAD83(2011) / UTM Zone 18N
**Area:** ~2.04 km² · **Points:** 2.21 million · **Density:** ~1.08 pts/m²
**Classifications:** Ground · Unclassified · Water · Rail · Bridge Deck · Noise

This tile covers a section of Manhattan adjacent to Central Park. The vertical range (−10 to +385 m) captures both below-grade infrastructure and the surrounding high-rise skyline. Points are colored by LiDAR classification — rotate and zoom to explore the urban 3D structure.

## Small Tree Plot

**Source:** USGS 3DEP · WGS 84 / UTM Zone 6N
**Area:** ~399 m² · **Points:** 10.4 thousand · **Density:** ~26 pts/m²
**Classifications:** Ground · Vegetation · Unclassified

A high-density scan of a small tree stand (~20 m × 20 m). At 26 pts/m² this tile resolves individual tree crowns and branching structure in detail. Points reach up to 17 m above ground. All points are shown — no subsampling.
